what_it_measured.text: This study evaluated the therapeutic efficacy and underlying molecular mechanisms of recombinant human thymosin β4 (rhTβ4) in a murine model of lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced endotoxemia.
Both mechanisms may contribute to the observed anti-inflammatory phenotype, and elucidating their relative roles represents an important objective for future investigation.

This study evaluated the therapeutic efficacy and underlying molecular mechanisms of recombinant human thymosin β4 (rhTβ4) in a murine model of lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced endotoxemia.
To evaluate the efficacy of rhTβ4 in attenuating LPS-induced oxidative stress and inflammation, we assessed mitochondrial homeostasis and ROS dynamics (Figure 3A).
(B) Cognitive performance assessed by the novel object recognition test and Y-maze test in Control, LPS-, and LPS + rhTβ4-treated mice.
Treatment with rhTβ4 significantly improved survival outcomes, conferring an 80% survival rate at 72 h post-challenge and doubling the median survival time from 48 to 72 h (Figure 1B).
